title: Gardenio — Killed-Mid-Work Agents (involuntary deaths)

panels.title: About this board

options.content: **Every series here should trend to zero.** An involuntary death is an agent that did not choose to stop: `context_cancelled` (node reclaimed under it), `context_cancelled_unclaimed` (killed before it claimed work), an OOMKill, or a node that disappeared. Families split *how* they died; the role/project breakdowns say *which workload class pays for it*. Spikes here are lost work and wasted spend, and the node-reclaim panel is the one wired to an alert.

panels.title: Killed mid-work — the prove-it-stopped signal (ka-0000008189)
Involuntary deaths (last 24h)
panels.description: Total agents killed mid-work in the last 24h across selected env/project. This is the headline number Matt wants to drive to zero. Sourced from gardenio_agent_involuntary_deaths_total, which increments only when an agent bead closes with a `_involuntary` close_reason (a claimed task was in flight). Empty-branch liveness: the `or vector(0)` fallback is gated on `up{component="agents"} == 1`, so a green 0 appears only while the controller exporter is actually being scraped — if it goes dark the panel stays empty and says so instead of painting a reassuring zero.

defaults.noValue: exporter dark — the controller scrape is down, so this panel cannot tell a real 0 from a counter that is simply gone

panels.title: Involuntary deaths per hour, by family
panels.description: increase()-per-hour of gardenio_agent_involuntary_deaths_total split by death family. family enum: stop_gate_cooldown (Claude exited mid-turn — account rotation/churn), stop_gate_escape_hatch, stop_gate_rate_limited, context_cancelled (pod SIGTERM'd mid-turn with a claimed issue — node drain/rollout/Spot reclaim), context_cancelled_unclaimed (SIGTERM'd busy-but-taskless agent — C9 ka-0000001146), other (novel shape). A fix landing should visibly bend the relevant family's curve toward the floor.

panels.title: Involuntary deaths per day, total (7d trend — should trend to zero)
panels.description: Daily count of killed-mid-work agents. This is the canonical 'have we stopped it' chart: as the root-cause fixes (P0 ka-0000003464 family + residual ka-0000001718) land and roll out, this bar should shrink to zero and stay there. Panel is pinned to a fixed 7-day window (timeFrom: 7d) with a 1-day query step (interval: 1d) so each bar is one discrete day's deaths — NOT a rolling cumulative curve. This override makes the panel show 7 per-day bars regardless of the dashboard time picker (fixes ka-0000005444: at the 24h picker the old rolling increase()[1d] read as an ever-climbing cumulative line).

panels.description: Which agent roles are getting killed mid-work. crew/thread on the shared pool are the usual victims of account-rotation churn.

panels.title: Node-reclaim sentinel — what AgentNodeReclaimDeaths fires on (WS4 ka-0000007155)
Node-reclaim deaths (context_cancelled, last 1h)
panels.description: The exact quantity the AgentNodeReclaimDeaths alert thresholds on: sum(increase(gardenio_agent_involuntary_deaths_total{family="context_cancelled"}[1h])). family=context_cancelled is a pod SIGTERM'd mid-turn by a forced node teardown (Spot / AWS health / interruption-queue) — the class WS1 graceful-drain (!5577) + WS2 node-churn cut (!5578) keep rare. Red at the alert default threshold (2/h): if this stat is red, the sentinel is firing and node reclaims are outpacing WS1/WS2. Work is NOT lost (drain nudge + S3 salvage) — the harm is a cold-resume; pivot to the resume-latency board (dashboard link, top-right) to see how fast it came back. Empty-branch liveness: the `or vector(0)` fallback is gated on `up{component="agents"} == 1`, so a green 0 appears only while the controller exporter is actually being scraped — if it goes dark the panel stays empty and says so instead of painting a reassuring zero.

defaults.noValue: exporter dark — the controller scrape is down, so this panel cannot tell a real 0 from a counter that is simply gone

panels.title: Node-reclaim deaths per hour vs alert threshold
panels.description: context_cancelled deaths-per-hour over time, with the AgentNodeReclaimDeaths alert threshold (2/h) drawn as a red reference line. When the bars cross the line for the alert `for` window (15m), the sentinel fires. This is the WS1/WS2 regression story: the bars should sit at or near the floor and only blip on a lone AWS health event; a sustained climb above the line means node reclaims are hitting agents faster than the graceful-drain + churn-reduction work keeps them rare.

panels.title: Unclaimed mid-turn kills — previously uncounted (C9 ka-0000001146)
Unclaimed kills (context_cancelled_unclaimed, last 24h)
panels.description: Agents SIGTERM'd (node drain / rollout / Spot reclaim) with tool calls recorded on the bead but NO claimed issue task — thread agents mid-answer, gardeners mid-watchdog-pass, crew doing pre-claim research. Before C9 (ka-0000001146) these closed as plain context_cancelled and never reached the deaths counter at all. Counted as their own family — NOT folded into context_cancelled — so the node-reclaim sentinel keeps its claimed-issue precision (MR !5571 / ka-0000008254). Caveat: total_tool_calls is bead-lifetime cumulative, so a warm-parked thread agent killed between turns lands here too; read this as an upper bound on taskless mid-turn kills. Empty-branch liveness: the `or vector(0)` fallback is gated on `up{component="agents"} == 1`, so a green 0 appears only while the controller exporter is actually being scraped — if it goes dark the panel stays empty and says so instead of painting a reassuring zero.

panels.title: Unclaimed kills per hour, by role
panels.description: context_cancelled_unclaimed deaths-per-hour split by role — shows WHO the previously-invisible kills hit. Expect thread + gardener roles to dominate (they rarely hold a claimed issue), which is exactly why the claimed-issue-only classification missed them. A node-churn event shows up here as a synchronized spike alongside the context_cancelled sentinel above.

panels.title: Agent OOMKills — what AgentOOMKilled fires on (Track D, ka-0000001509)
Agent OOMKills (last 1h)
panels.description: The signal the AgentOOMKilled alert thresholds on: sum(increase(gardenio_agent_lifecycle_events_total{event="oom_killed"}[1h])). The controller status reporter emits this on every kubelet OOMKilled container termination on an agent pod (reporter.go recordPodLifecycleMetrics). Killed runs are auto-salvaged to S3 (harm is a cold-resume, not lost work); a sustained rate means the memory limit is too tight or a run is leaking. Red at 1/h. Pivot to the VPA right-sizing board (working-set vs limit) to size the fix. Empty-branch liveness: the `or vector(0)` fallback is gated on `up{component="agents"} == 1`, so a green 0 appears only while the controller exporter is actually being scraped — if it goes dark the panel stays empty and says so instead of painting a reassuring zero.

panels.title: OOMKills per hour, by project/role
panels.description: Per-(project,role) OOMKill rate over time — the AgentOOMKilled alert groups by (project,role) so the firing series names who is OOMing. Bars should sit at the floor; a sustained climb for one role means that role's agents are under-provisioned (widen the memory limit / VPA minAllowed) or leaking memory within a run.

panels.title: Node lifecycle churn — what AgentNodeLifecycleEvents fires on (Track D, ka-0000001509)
Agent nodes gone (last 1h)
panels.description: The signal the AgentNodeLifecycleEvents alert thresholds on: sum(increase(gardenio_node_lifecycle_events_total{reason="terminated"}[1h])) — one count per agent-pool node that went away, so this reads as NODES/h (ka-0000005966). Emitted by the controller node-lifecycle collector (internal/nodelifecycle), which sweeps the cluster Node API. terminated = node vanished from the listing (graceful drain OR abrupt Spot/AWS-health/interruption-queue reclaim); it fires once per node regardless of path. The alert used to sum disrupting|deleting|terminated, but a single graceful teardown walks all three edges (~3 events per node gone), tripping the old per-node 6/h threshold on ~2 clean consolidations/h — see the per-reason breakdown panel for the teardown path. Node churn is expected background; a sustained rate is the leading indicator before it cold-resumes agents. Red at the alert threshold (15/h, calibrated up from the 6/h placeholder in ka-0000005205 to sit above busy-fleet burst-drain). Empty-branch liveness: the `or vector(0)` fallback is gated on `count(gardenio_agent_node_count) > 0`, the gauge the same collector sweep overwrites every pass — so a green 0 means the sweep ran and saw no teardown, not that the collector stopped reporting.

defaults.noValue: exporter dark — the controller scrape is down, so this panel cannot tell a real 0 from a counter that is simply gone

panels.title: Node lifecycle events per hour, by reason
panels.description: Per-reason node lifecycle rate over time, with the AgentNodeLifecycleEvents alert threshold (15/h) as a red reference line. The alert counts the terminated reason only (once-per-node, ka-0000005966); disrupting/deleting/not_ready are shown here for the teardown-path breakdown but are NOT counted by the alert (a graceful teardown emits all three, and not_ready is a Ready-condition health flap). disrupting/deleting leading terminated = graceful teardown; a terminated spike with little disrupting = abrupt reclaim (Spot/AWS health). Correlate with the node-reclaim sentinel above: churn up + reclaim-deaths up = agents being caught (verify the WS1 drain nudge is on).
